attributes.residual: The loop body is now byte-identical to target through the call: `lwz r3,40(rP); mr r4,r27; lwz r0,36(rP); lwzx r3,r3,r31; add r3,r0,r3; bl stricmp` -- the previous operand/register split at +0x3c and +0x40 is GONE. Everything that remains sits in ONE block, the six-instruction loop prologue at +0x10..+0x2c, and is two mechanisms both screened source-unreachable: (1) LIVE-ZERO-REMAT -- target issues `li r30,0` (i = 0) and then materialises the strength-reduced byte-offset IV by COPYING that live zero, `addi r31,r30,0`; ours rematerialises it, `li r28,0; li r31,0`. That is exactly claim.law.live-zero-copy-vs-remat-is-allocator-not-source, and it is the same signature the run-36 movieplayer record filed a capability request for. (2) A 3-cycle recolor of the surviving volatile webs, ours r29/r30/r28 == target r28/r29/r30. Both are register-field differences at equal instruction counts, so the pair is exactly what copy_register_fields plus a live-zero-copy normalisation would absorb. NOTE the TU already carries two other members of the SAME live-zero/IV-init class -- DrawStringTextMLines (target `addi r27,r30,0` vs our `slwi r27,r30,2`) and FontInit (target `addi r30,r27,0` vs our `slwi`) -- so btext.c holds THREE instances and is the densest customer for that capability found so far.
